title: When the Internet Goes Down, Your Security System Should Not
description: Most organisations assume their security system will keep working when connectivity drops. In practice, many do not — because the system was installed without a fallback. A resilient monitoring setup uses primary Ethernet for day-to-day operation and automatically switches to 4G LTE when that connection fails, keeping alarm reporting, video streaming and remote access running without interruption. With communicators like the Inner Range T4000 Pro now offering dual-SIM failover and VPN support built in, there is no longer a meaningful reason to leave your site vulnerable to a network outage. Here is how we design for continuity.

title: Your Physical Security System Is an IT Asset — Is Your IT Team Treating It That Way?
description: IP cameras, access controllers, alarm panels — everything is on the network now. But in most organisations, physical security devices sit outside the IT governance framework. No patch management. No visibility into firmware versions. No ownership over network credentials. ASIS International flagged this IT/OT governance gap as a growing priority for security leaders this month — and for good reason. When a networked CCTV system becomes the entry point for a ransomware attack, the question of who owns that device becomes urgent very fast. Here is how Wellington and Auckland organisations should be thinking about it.
